title: Katelyn Lesse – Evolving Claude APIs for Agents, Anthropic
talk_summary: Anthropic's developer platform lead describes three API-level levers for agent performance: exposing model capabilities (thinking budgets, tool use), actively managing the context window (MCP, memory tool, context editing), and giving the model a sandboxed computer plus 'skills' folders of scripts/instructions. It is mostly product framing, but the context-management and skills mechanisms are concrete and copyable.

takeaways.technique: Clear stale tool results from context
takeaways.what_they_do: Context editing drops old tool results from the window because they are large and rarely relevant to later turns, while a memory tool keeps that content outside the window and pulls it back only when needed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: our first iteration of our context editing is just clearing out old tool results ... tool results from past calls are not necessarily super relevant
takeaways.numbers: 39% performance bump on internal evals when memory tool + context editing combined

takeaways.technique: Client-side memory files the model writes and retrieves
takeaways.what_they_do: A memory tool is a client-side filesystem: Claude decides what to store for later and pulls it back into context only when relevant, keeping durable knowledge out of the window.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we introduced a memory tool to help you actually keep context outside of the window that Claude knows how to pull back into the window only when it actually needs it

takeaways.technique: Skills as folders of scripts + instructions selected by description
takeaways.what_they_do: Skills are folders of scripts, instructions and resources; the model picks one to load based on the task and the skill's description, then runs it inside its sandbox.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Skills are basically just folders of scripts, instructions, and resources that Claude has access to and can decide to run within its sandbox environment

takeaways.technique: Hosted code-execution sandbox with session persistence
takeaways.what_they_do: A code execution tool runs model-written code in secure, orchestrated containers on their servers, and sessions persist so work continues while the user is away.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we needed to solve or container orchestration at scale ... and we needed session persistence

takeaways.what_they_do: Thinking is exposed as an API knob with a token budget so callers choose long reasoning for hard problems and short answers for easy ones.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can tell Claude how many tokens to essentially spend on thinking
